message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5

    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [22]

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v3
        with:
          version: 10.28.1

      - name: Setup Node ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --ignore-scripts

      - name: build packages
        run: pnpm build

      - name: Run tests
        run: pnpm test

      # Feel free to remove this step if you don't want to run the README.md
      - name: Run README.md
        run: pnpm dlx ezx@0.0.18 -k --verbose README.md
",
  "rationale": "The workflow has no job-level timeout, so a hung or runaway job can consume unbounded runner time. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is supported by the measured experiment experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508, which showed adding timeout-minutes reduced elapsed time and bounds runaway consumption, and by the pattern catalogue entry pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT. Repository CI history shows successful runs complete in roughly one minute, so a five-minute budget gives ample operational headroom and does not risk false timeouts on valid slow runs. All existing steps (checkout, pnpm setup, install, build, test, README run) are preserved, so build and test coverage is unchanged.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}
